name: Pre-Prep
stage: Early Years Foundation Stage and Key Stage 1
tagline: Wonder first. Then words, numbers and the confidence to use them.
intro: Our youngest girls learn in bright, calm rooms that open straight onto the garden. Days are built around play with purpose: stories read aloud, counting with conkers, songs in three languages and a great deal of mud. Small classes and two adults in every room mean each child is known, noticed and gently stretched.

quotes.text: She comes home with a new question every day — and usually with paint on her sleeve.
We teach reading the way you'd teach a friend a secret: carefully, joyfully, and one sound at a time.
The garden is our second classroom. Some days it is our first.

wellbeing: Every morning begins with a welcome circle where each girl is greeted by name. Key adults stay with children through the day, settling-in is unhurried, and we share a short note home each week so families always know the shape of their daughter's days.
beyond: Weekly forest school in the Wild Wood
Little Chefs in the teaching kitchen
Story-and-pyjamas evenings
Swimming from Reception
Harvest festival and the winter lantern walk

name: Prep
tagline: The years when curiosity becomes capability.
intro: In Prep, girls build the habits that carry them through school: reading widely, writing with care, reasoning out loud and trying again. Specialist teachers for science, music, languages, art and sport join from Year 3, while a form tutor remains the steady centre of each girl's day.

quotes.text: Prep is where girls learn that being wrong is just the first draft of being right.
My daughter now argues with me about the water cycle. I'm told this is progress.
The best lessons end with more questions than they began with.

wellbeing: Each girl belongs to a form, a house and a buddy pair with an older pupil. Tutors meet every child one-to-one each half-term, and our pastoral team keeps a light, watchful eye on friendships — the thing that matters most to an eight-year-old.
beyond: Junior choir and string ensemble
Chess, coding and LEGO engineering clubs
First residential trip in Year 4
Inter-house sports and the spring swimming gala
The Year 6 enterprise market

name: Upper School
tagline: Depth, independence, and room to discover what she loves.
intro: Upper School widens every horizon. Girls study the full breadth of the curriculum through Key Stage 3 before choosing nine or ten IGCSE subjects in Year 10. Teaching is ambitious and personal: we want girls to master their subjects and also to own their learning — to plan, revise, ask for help and lead.

quotes.text: IGCSE gave her a reason to read beyond the syllabus — and the confidence to say so.
We teach to the top and scaffold for everyone. That's not a slogan; it's a lesson plan.
Upper School is when the girls start teaching us.

wellbeing: Every girl has a tutor who stays with her group across Upper School. A weekly wellbeing curriculum covers sleep, study habits, digital life, relationships and resilience. Our counsellor and school nurse are on site every day, and older girls train as peer listeners.
beyond: Model United Nations and debating
Horizon Fellowship expeditions from Year 9
The Atelier design studio
Orchestra, chamber choir and the school musical
Fixtures in eight sports against regional schools

name: Sixth Form
tagline: Two years to think like a scholar and act like a leader.
intro: Sixth Formers choose three or four A Levels, add an Extended Project of their own design, and take on real leadership across the school. Seminar-sized classes feel more like university than school, and every girl is guided through her next step — in India or abroad — by a dedicated futures adviser.

quotes.text: The Extended Project taught me to manage my own time. The A Levels taught me everything else.
We treat Sixth Formers as the young adults they are — with high trust and higher expectations.
University applications are a conversation that starts in Year 12, not a panic in Year 13.

wellbeing: Sixth Formers have their own study centre and common room, a tutor who meets them weekly, and protected time for rest, sport and service. Our counsellor runs sessions on managing pressure and transition, and girls choose a staff mentor in their area of interest.
beyond: Head Girl team and prefect roles
Leading clubs and teaching younger pupils
Horizon Fellowship capstone project
Internship fortnight in Year 12
University preparation evenings and alumnae talks
